title: PRESSER | Chris Beard, Ben Henshall & Budd Clark - Postgame vs. BYU (11-24-26)
text: All right, please welcome Miss to the media room. Uh we've head coach Chris Beard, Bud Clark, and Ben Henchel. Uh coach, down 14 at half, came back for for a big win. What did you see from your team this morning? [snorts] >> Yeah, I think from a coaching standpoint, um just trying to explain to the guys coming into this tournament that it's not going to be a matter of if adversity comes, it's going to be when. And then just always looking forward to uh as a coach how your guys respond. We create a lot of adversity internally in practice and situations like that, but this is the first time we gotten popped this regular season. Uh so I thought our guys did a good job at the end of the first half uh not panicking, didn't didn't let it balloon up. We won the last two possessions of the first half. Then the message at halftime was to kind of reset and get back to our original game plan, which I thought we did. So tell of two halves. Uh BYU gave us all we could handle in the first half. I thought we flipped the script on them. um low turnover game for us combined with uh multiple guys in double digit scoring that kind of offset the rebounding uh disadvantage, but it's a good win for us. Um we came to Maui to win three games and so um pleased that we'll have an opportunity to do that tomorrow. >> Any questions for uh Ben or Bud? >> Um yeah, this is for both of you going in as coach said to the second half. You guys put on gas to the pedal. What would you say to your first half self? If you could go back in there, what would you switch your mindset to going to that first? >> Um, I think we had the right mindset coming in. Uh, we wanted to set the tone defensively. Um, I think we gave up too many easy points early on. Um, I think that's something we could have cleaned up, but uh, I think really like the way we came out, competed in the second half. Um, I think if we can bring that from the start like we did in the first game, uh, we're going to be a tough team to beat. >> Yeah, like Ben said, just come out like that from the start. Uh, just always carry that chip on our shoulder. Uh, we are we all guys with a story. We all want to carry a chip on our shoulder the first four minutes. Just come out with a intensity, uh, energy, uh, and be ourselves, cause turnovers on defense. That's what we are. >> Any other questions for the players? >> All right, guys. Thanks for being here. We'll let you go. Any questions for coach? >> Coach, [snorts] you already said it. You were proud of your team in the second half and they kind of talked about the first half, but what would you try to do differently to coach them to start right away? Cuz first game yesterday, you were you guys were on fire going right at the jump was today. Did you guys relax a little bit because you went so hard or what was that that difference? Cuz I mean BYU gave you a run for your money, but I saw a different team than I saw from yesterday in the start. Yeah, respectfully, I I don't see it like that. You know, I've never liked the coach who gets up here and talks about um what they didn't do or couldn't do. Let's talk about the opponent. Um the way BYU played in the first half, especially a little underman without their playmaker, um that's a Big 12 championship contending team. So, um obviously there's some things we can clean up. Um but I think a lot of our mistakes were because of BYU, so I give them a lot of credit in the first half. Coach, was there anything specific you saw from BYU in the first half that you could go into halftime knowing you could attack in the second half? >> Yeah, I thought they were the most aggressive team. Uh, you know, Coach Knight said it best, victory favors the most aggressive team. And they were um they were going downhill. Um, they're putting a lot of pressure on our defense and the officials to make 50/50 calls. And so I thought for the, you know, first four minutes of the game, five minutes of the game, BYU was the most aggressive team. So at halftime it was just a um you know a calm reminder to our team that man we're in a big boy game here. We're in a Maui Invitational. We're playing against a team that is in the top 25. Uh let's don't have any regrets here. You know two types of regret. Regret of discipline, regret of um you know discipline. Uh we don't we don't have regret. You know if um and so that was the big message at halftime really wasn't a yelling, screaming, kicking trash cans. It was just like you know especially to the veteran players. Let's calm down. We knew how important the first four minutes of the second half was. I've always thought that you got to win those four minutes. I don't have a 15-point play, but if you can just win that first four minutes by a basket or two, then it can settle down into a game. And that's exactly what we do. >> Coach over here. >> You always talk about you always talk about player teams. This looks like a player team and this is outside looking in. Bud, Clark, Roman. Can you speak about how playerled teams just work out better in this world? Yeah, I'm enjoying coaching this team so far. Um, and our leadership comes in a lot of different ways. Bud's an alpha, controls the game. Ilas is a calm personality playmaker. Roman's a competitor, a fighter. Ben's a fighter. Uh, many other guys, guys that aren't in the rotation right now are leading this team as well, and how they practice every day and their attitude, effort, and body language. So, it's early in the season. We're a work in progress. Uh, but we do appear to be a team that will really rely on player leadership as the season goes on. All right. Anything else? Yep. One more. Coach [snorts] >> coach, have you [clears throat] discovered the roles just through practices or some of the preseason games? Cuz the team really had strong roles, Roman hitting the boards, you know, Elias scored well yesterday, but just had these beautiful fast break assists. I mean, the roles are strong coming in different forms. I mean, is it just now or you have you been kind of slowly discovering it? >> Yeah, I appreciate that question and that compliment in the question because that's what we really strive for. You know, this is college basketball. It's a team sport. We've got a team very similar to most teams in the country where we have a lot of players that maybe were last year's leading scorer, last year's leading rebounder. We've asked these guys to check the ego at the door and let's play for Miss. Um, one example off the top of my head, I thought Roman Ceppa played like an absolute warrior today. although scoring wasn't in uh his neighborhood today, the way he rebounded and defended. And so we got a lot of guys that are unselfish. We got a lot of guys that play for Old Miss. We really don't care much about the stat sheet. Our our team's a work in progress. It's early in the season. We work on role definition every single day. Um but I agree with you and I appreciate the compliment. I thought our guys played like a team today in the second half. Thank you.
